title: Electrophysiological signatures underlying variability in human memory consolidation: raw intracranial EEG (learning and sleep TMR)
description: Raw stereo-EEG (intracranial EEG) recordings from 11 patients with medically refractory temporal lobe epilepsy at Sanbo Brain Hospital, Beijing. Data were acquired during learning of object-location associations and during targeted memory reactivation (TMR) with sounds in NREM sleep. The dataset supports investigation of electrophysiological signatures that explain variability in human memory consolidation. It is a lossless BIDS re-packaging of the authors' Zenodo release.
methods_description: Depth electrodes with 8-16 contacts were recorded on a Nicolet system (128 channels, 512 Hz). In the learning task, participants learned 50 object-location associations on a grid until reaching criterion. After a pre-sleep test, 25 cued sounds and 25 control sounds were presented during NREM stage 2/3 sleep, detected with scalp EEG. Original MATLAB arrays were converted to BrainVision float32 without filtering, resampling or re-referencing.
